29/12/2019

Results of ultrasound explained - impalpable, focal well-circumscribed solid
parenchymal lesion in R breast, 1cm in diameter consistent with fibroadenoma. Pt
informed of benign impalpable fibroadenomas (common for age group, no evidence
of premalignancy).

Pt clearly distressed over possible link to cancer

Referred to breast surgeon, Dr Anthony Hargreaves, for further evaluation.

diagnosis of benign fibroadenoma.
Results of biopsy: benign lesion confirmed. Pt advised by surgeon - surgery not
required. Clinical observation by periodic ultrasound assessments ongoing.

Pt insists removal is necessary, requests new referral to female breast surgeon for
turther opinion.

Dear Dr. Chamber,
Re: Ms Heidi Walsh

I am writing to refer Ms. Walsh,
a 20-year-old who has recently been diagnosed with bening fibroadenoma
in the right breast. She requires further assessment.
On 27-12-2019, Ms. Walsh
presented at the surgery with tenderness and lumpiness in the right breast,
associated
with some tenderness in the left breast. On examination, her physical
examination was normal but an ultrasound of both breasts Therefore, an
ultrasound of both breasts was ordered.
 
Two days later, the result of
the utrasoune (continued from previous paragraph)revealed
an impalpable, focal, well-circumscribed solid paranchymal lestion
in the right breast, associated with a 1 cm-diameter fibroadenoma. As a result,
she has been referred to you have to give the name of the surgeon the
a breast surgeon for further evaluation. You need to state that you
referred her because she was worried it might be cancer.
Today, Ms. Walsh attended the
clinic following a surgical referral. She was anxious. The sutgeon advised
undergoing did an ultrasound-guided percutanous core biopsy te
eonfirm which confirmed the diagnosis and he advised against
surgery, recommending . Therefore, the surgeon advised her to underge
continuous
clinical monitoring through periodic ultrasound evaluations. She requests a
new
referral to the a female breast surgeon for the removal of the
lesions.

New paragraph Please
note, Ms. Walsh has a positive family history of breast cancer in her mother,
which
was successfully treated by mastectomy and axillary dissection, and she
drinks 2 units of alcohol
per week why does the reader need to know this?

could assess Ms. Walsh, as you think appropriate More detail for the request
